Chingy sits down with DJ Vlad for a candid look back at the Sidney Starr controversy, including Starr’s later admission that she lied about an alleged relationship to gain attention in the entertainment industry. The conversation revisits the viral photo, Chingy’s claim that the rumors hurt his career, and how Starr’s public profile later grew through reality TV appearances on Zeus and *Baddies*. Vlad also brings up his past interview with Starr, comments about transgender disclosure, and a debate with Van Lathan about safety, consent, and straight men being misled. Chingy recalls the 2004 porn awards incident, photos with performers in body paint, and why he believed the situation felt set up. The interview also touches on Twista, Vegas, music industry rumors, and Vlad’s comparison between Starr’s polished on-camera appearance and a very different-looking mugshot.

--------

Hit-Boy sits with Vlad and Elliott Wilson for a candid look at the producer’s grind, including whether he’d sell beats to wack artists and how that early hustle shaped his career. The Grammy-winning hitmaker explains why he stopped being “precious” with tracks, how keeping thousands of ideas moving pushes him creatively, and why he now plays everything for everybody. The conversation touches on signature sounds from Dr. Dre, Pharrell, Timbaland and Lil Jon, the shift from regional styles to trap’s dominance, and the challenge of longevity in a viral era. Hit-Boy also reflects on making his own albums, working with Nas across multiple projects, memories around “Paris,” Guru, Jay-Z, Surf Club, South by Southwest in Austin, and the industry’s transition into Spotify and Apple Music streaming.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
--------
Judge Mathis joins VladTV to break down the federal fraud case against Daejon Love, the alleged fake NFL player accused of scamming more than 20 women out of $1.3 million by posing as a San Francisco 49ers quarterback and promising big investment returns. Vlad details Love’s flashy claims, from a supposed Gucci stake on Fifth Avenue to luxury cars, a Richard Mille watch, and a 49ers turkey giveaway flyer used to build credibility. Mathis compares the behavior to classic con games, recalls seeing gigolos in his courtroom, and explains why romance scams can carry serious prison time even without violence. The conversation also touches on Love’s alleged 18-year-old “financial advisor,” Trump’s meme coin controversy, Washington, D.C., and how fraud sentencing often plays out. Asked what Love could face if convicted or pleading guilty, Judge Mathis predicts around 10 years behind bars.

--------
Charleston White joins VladTV to analyze Allstar JR’s Detroit shooting case involving NBA Ben10, arguing that JR’s actions after allegedly gaining control of the gun could weaken a self-defense claim. Vlad recalls JR being arrested while on the way to a VladTV interview, shortly after the “Ben 10 Challenge” buzz and a new video release. The conversation examines bond, trial strategy, fingerprints, fleeing the scene, possession of a firearm as a convicted felon, and why continuing to shoot at people running away may shift a person from victim to suspect. White also compares law enforcement evidence tactics to cases like the Mo3 investigation and “ghost dope” prosecutions. Vlad shares his own past experience with an attack to discuss adrenaline, excessive force, and how judges and juries evaluate self-defense after the immediate threat ends.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/fjE20W3ouPQ
--------
Attorney and online legal commentator Moe Gangat sits down with Vlad to address Tekashi 6ix9ine’s viral criticism that his high-profile trial predictions are “always wrong.” In the clip, 6ix9ine blasts Gangat over past commentary involving Tory Lanez and claims about whether Lil Durk could come home, accusing him of chasing fame and trying to control the narrative around rappers, snitching, gangs, and cooperators.

Gangat pushes back, arguing that Tekashi avoids responding to the substance of his legal points and is using the moment for views. He explains that his social media presence functions like advertising for his contingency-fee law practice, where he represents clients in serious injury lawsuits and police brutality cases. The conversation also touches on Rainbet, online clout, legal media, and why criminal cases involving hip-hop artists continue to dominate YouTube search and social media debate.

---------
Chingy sits down with Vlad to address the latest news surrounding Sidney Starr, who has reportedly been jailed without bond on charges including aggravated child molestation, sexual battery against a child under 16, and sodomy involving an alleged 13-year-old victim. The St. Louis rapper revisits the viral controversy that began after a photo at a Chicago show during his Disturbing tha Peace era, when Starr later claimed they had a relationship—an allegation Chingy has long denied.

He explains how the rumor spread through MediaTakeOut, The Breakfast Club, blogs, and social media, costing him a potential record deal and even a Chingy-branded Mastercard opportunity. Chingy also reflects on why he didn’t keep publicly fighting the claim, how he considered defamation action, and how the situation affected his career, public image, and interactions with fans. Vlad also recalls believing Chingy’s denial from the beginning.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/oJzes6G-Jac
--------
DJ Vlad sits down with Hit-Boy for a candid conversation about loyalty, family, and the risks of chasing a rap career later in life. The discussion opens with Vlad referencing his interview with Brian “Glaze” Gibbs, the Queens drug era, and the Jam Master Jay murder case, using it as a cautionary example of older street figures staying tied to dangerous situations. From there, Hit-Boy breaks down spending over $1 million—around $1.3 million by his count—on his father’s music campaign, including housing, clothes, travel, video shoots, and photo shoots.

Hit-Boy explains why he pushed the project, how the album A Game Stays With You gained attention, and why bonding with his dad and son mattered. Elliott Wilson, Master P, and 2 Chainz come up as the conversation explores father-son dynamics, age in hip-hop, and whether money can repair family trauma.
